findings: ETT.tex:1792. « Since X is non-singular, ψ is a local diffeomorphism » needs Σ to be a C¹ hypersurface transverse to X. The theorem's Σ is any Cauchy surface, a topological set (DEC-14). Topologically the step is the continuity of the hitting time, which is equivalent to J^±(Σ) closed (Causal.Causality.IsCausalFlow.isClosed_iff_exists_isCauchySplitting). The paper gets that closedness only afterwards, from ψ (lem:Sigma_separe, l.2067, « ψ being a homeomorphism » l.2079). It holds without ψ (T-ett-sigma-separe), and then the « Moreover » holds for every causal flow at every causal, Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold (Causal.SingularRowsSplitting.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow; abstractly Causal.Causality.SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow). Neither C¹, transversality, parallelism at sing(M), global hyperbolicity nor connectedness is needed. The openness the paper asserts (l.1792) is a theorem (isOpenMap_of_vecteurFlow). Of lem:vecteur the proof uses only a complete continuous flow with causal orbits and no fixed point. (The smoothness gap was disclosed in Causal.Splitting's SCOPE; it is not yet among this row's findings.)

ETT.tex:2062–2064 against l.1778–1795, order of the results. lem:Sigma_separe takes ψ from theo:geroch_sing and derives its « In particular » from ψ being a homeomorphism (l.2079). In the topological setting the dependency runs the other way: the ψ-free « In particular » (J^±(Σ) closed) is what makes ψ a homeomorphism. The author may want to state the ψ-free « In particular » before theo:geroch_sing, or inside the proof of its « Moreover ».

ETT.tex:1763 (proof of lem:vecteur), at E₀. The flow of the vertical field X_0, read as the τ-translation of Causal.E0, is null at every point of E₀, not only on the singular line. r is constant along its orbits and ≪ asks r₁ < r₂ (Causal.SingularRowsSplitting.not_lt_tauFlow). More generally no flow of a singular flat spacetime with a BTZ point is chronal. A chronal flow gives every point a chronological past, and a BTZ point has I⁻ = ∅ (Causal.Causality.IsChronalFlow.Iminus_nonempty, SingularFlatAxioms.not_isChronalFlow; at M, Causal.SingularRowsSplitting.not_hasChronalCausalFlow, which needs neither Hausdorffness nor second countability). The paper is not wrong here: l.1755 says « future causal ». The consequence is that the classical argument, a timelike flow closes J^±(Σ), is unavailable as soon as sing₀(M) ≠ ∅. The step at l.1792 must then rest on the « In particular » of lem:Sigma_separe.
questions: ETT.tex:1751–1758, 1788–1789: what the « Moreover » uses of the C¹ field X of lem:vecteur and its complete flow Φ. Reading taken: its C⁰ content only, Causal.Splitting's IsCausalFlow. That is a complete continuous ℝ-action (mathlib's Flow ℝ M) whose orbits are inextensible future causal curves over ℝ in the DEC-6 sense, with no fixed point (« non-singular »). « C¹ » and « parallel to the singular line » are not modelled, and neither is used. IsCausalFlow.of_causalCurveIn shows that « non-singular and causal » already give inextensible orbits on a Hausdorff space, which matches l.1793.

ETT.tex:1763: « the vertical vector field X_κ of E_κ » for κ = 0. Reading taken: ∂_τ in the coordinates of Causal.E0, so its flow is the τ-translation E0.tauShift (tauFlow). No proof uses this reading: tauFlow is proved a causal flow directly, and it is the witness of VecteurFlow and of IsCausalFlow at E₀ whatever X_0 is. It rests on OQ-34, OQ-35.

findings: ETT.tex:2063–2066. The two equalities J^±(Σ) = ψ(Σ × ℝ_±) need neither global hyperbolicity nor ψ being a homeomorphism. For any causal flow φ of a causal spacetime and any acausal Cauchy surface Σ, J⁺(Σ) = {φ_t(x) : x ∈ Σ, t ≥ 0} and J⁻(Σ) = {φ_t(x) : x ∈ Σ, t ≤ 0} as sets (Causal.Causality.IsCausalFlow.Jplus_eq_image, Jminus_eq_image). This is model-free and uses no closedness. The proof goes through the hitting time and uses the acausality of Σ, not the concatenated curve and the Cauchy property of the editorial proof (l.2075–2077). For singular flat spacetimes the gain is in the route, not in the class: in the paper global hyperbolicity follows from theo:geroch_sing (iii)⇒(i) (l.1771–1777; OQ-32's tagged sorry in Lean).
questions: ETT.tex:2064: « the homeomorphism of Theorem theo:geroch_sing ». The paper's X, hence its ψ, is not unique. Reading taken: every homeomorphism ψ with ψ(x, t) = φ_t(x) for some causal flow φ (sigma_separe_of_isCausalFlow quantifies over all of them), so the paper's ψ is covered for any choice of the field of lem:vecteur.

kb_proposals: Geroch's « Moreover » from any causal flow: Causal.Causality.SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow. From a causal SFA spacetime, IsCausalFlow φ and a Cauchy surface S it gives ψ (x, t) = φ t x, a Cauchy splitting, with J^±(S) closed from sigma_separe_of_isCausal. At M it is Causal.SingularRowsSplitting.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow. At a causal SFA spacetime VecteurFlow and IsCausalFlow are equivalent (VecteurFlow.toFlow / .isCausalFlow, IsCausalFlow.toVecteurFlow, nonempty_vecteurFlow_iff). State new splitting results with IsCausalFlow (T-ett-geroch-split-flow).

E₀'s τ-translation as a mathlib Flow: Causal.SingularRowsSplitting.tauFlow (tauFlow t x = (x.1 + t, x.2) by rfl), a causal flow (isCausalFlow_tauFlow). Its orbits are curves through E0.curveOn_of_continuousOn and E0.causalCurveOn_of_curveOn, with Le from E0.le_iff_closed at equal angles arg x.2; inextensibility comes from IsCausalFlow.of_causalCurveIn (inextensible_of_flow). The flow is null (not_lt_tauFlow). vecteurFlow_e0 is a VecteurFlow at E₀ and tauFlow_split splits E₀ along every Cauchy surface (T-ett-geroch-split-flow).

No chronal flow once some point has I⁻ = ∅: Causal.Causality.IsChronalFlow.Iminus_nonempty (model-free), SingularFlatAxioms.not_isChronalFlow / not_hasChronalCausalFlow, and at M SingularRowsSplitting.not_hasChronalCausalFlow (no T2, no second countability). So exists_isCauchySplitting_of_isChronalFlow never applies with a BTZ point. Use the causal-flow form with sigma_separe_of_isCausal (T-ett-geroch-split-flow).

Flow-tube equalities with no closedness: IsCausalFlow.Jplus_eq_image and Jminus_eq_image give J^±(S) = {φ t x | x ∈ S, ±t ≥ 0} for any causal flow, causal C and acausal Cauchy S, by the hitting time (T-ett-geroch-split-flow).

IsCausalFlow and Causal.Splitting's Target 2 (the hitting-time splitting) are model-free but stranded in a module that imports Causal.Flat.IsomCausal (with Minkowski, Static, GXStructure and the manifold/ODE parts of mathlib in its closure). Hoisting them (kb/0047) would make CausalScaffold.SingularSplitting's closure model-free.
